rules.rationale: Halogen-dominated ionic salts have deep halide p valence bands and cation-derived conduction bands, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Oxide O 2p valence bands sit low in energy, so most stoichiometric oxides are wide-gap insulators.
Absence of partially filled d shells removes mid-gap and narrow d bands that collapse measured band gaps.
Light-element compounds have short bonds and large bonding-antibonding splitting, mechanistically favoring wide gaps.

skill.hypothesis: Pure domain prior: ionic, light, transition-metal-free halides and oxides maximize gaps. Fails if the catalog's oxides are dominated by mixed-valence transition-metal oxides whose d bands shrink gaps.
